skill.name: convex-migrate
skill.description: Stage schema changes on a deployed Convex app and use @convex-dev/migrations to update existing records. Verify the data before making new fields required.
skill.summary: Backfill existing Convex records before enforcing new schema requirements.
skill.author: convex

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no findings to adjudicate. Review found no evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or instructions to bypass authorization. The skill is prompt-only and guides live data changes, so users should confirm the target deployment before execution.

content.user_title: Migrate Convex Schemas and Backfill Data
content.value_statement: Making a new field required can cause existing Convex records to fail validation. This skill guides you through staging the field, backfilling records, and checking data before enforcing the new requirement.
actual_capabilities: Plan a schema change that introduces a new field as optional.
Draft a migration to populate or transform existing records.
Guide verification of row counts and record validity after a backfill.
Identify when the validator can make the new field required.
limitations: The skill provides instructions and does not bundle an executable migration.
Running a migration requires a Convex project and access to the intended deployment.
You must define how to populate values that cannot be inferred from existing records.
The workflow does not provide rollback instructions.

use_cases.title: Add a Required Field
use_cases.description: Stage a new profile field as optional and plan the backfill before making the field required.

use_cases.title: Transform Stored Values
use_cases.description: Draft a migration that maps legacy statuses into a new field. Flag any values that do not have an agreed mapping.

use_cases.title: Review a Deployment Plan
use_cases.description: Review the order of schema changes and identify the checks needed before enforcing the new validator.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Migration Order
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Plan a schema change before editing files.
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to add a required timezone field to my Convex profiles. Explain the migration order and what I should verify before making it required.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Field Backfill
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Prepare a migration for a known default.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Convex migration using @convex-dev/migrations to set missing email alert preferences to false. Preserve existing values and show where the field should remain optional. Do not run the migration.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Record Transformation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Move legacy values into a new field.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a backfill from the legacy status field into a new status field using my approved mapping. Flag unmapped values for review and propose checks for row counts and record validity.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Live Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Set verification criteria before a production change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my proposed Convex rollout from an optional field to a required field. Check the backfill order and list the evidence needed before tightening the validator. Do not deploy or run anything.

output_examples.input: How should I introduce an email alerts field on existing customer records?
output: Backfill missing values with the approved default and preserve existing preferences.
Compare row counts and verify that every record has a valid preference before making the field required.

output_examples.input: Can I make the new status field required if some legacy statuses are unmapped?
output: Keep the field optional while mappings are unresolved.
Review the unmapped values and agree on how to handle them.
Tighten the validator only after every record passes the proposed requirement.

best_practices: Deploy new fields as optional before backfilling existing records.
Confirm the target deployment and test the backfill outside production before running it on live data.
Compare row counts and verify record validity before making the field required.
anti_patterns: Make the new field required before existing records meet the requirement.
Run the backfill without confirming the target deployment.
Treat unchanged row counts as proof that the new field contains valid values.

faq.question: Which migration package does the skill use?
faq.answer: The workflow uses @convex-dev/migrations for data backfills and transformations.

faq.question: Why should a new field be optional first?
faq.answer: Existing records may lack the field. The optional validator lets those records remain valid until the backfill populates them.

faq.question: Does the skill automatically run the migration?
faq.answer: The skill contains instructions, not an executable migration. Execution depends on your assistant, project setup, and deployment access.

faq.question: Can I transform records instead of assigning a fixed default?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow supports transformations, but you must define the mapping and how to handle unexpected values.

faq.question: When can I make the field required?
faq.answer: Wait until the backfill completes and you verify that every existing record meets the stricter validator.

faq.question: Does the skill provide a rollback plan?
faq.answer: No. Prepare and test a recovery plan separately before changing live data.
